# Passenger Agent OS — Progress

Append-only worklog. Every agent adds an entry when it finishes a task — what shipped, what it learned, what it left behind. **Newest first — insert your entry at the top, never append at end-of-file** (L-003). `BOARD.md` holds current state; this holds history.

Entry format:

```
### YYYY-MM-DD — <agent> — <task id> <short title>
- **Did:** what actually changed (files, migrations, issue IDs)
- **Evidence:** build/test output, screenshots, review verdicts
- **Left behind:** follow-ups, known gaps, anything the next agent needs
```

### 2026-08-04 — product — T-062/PAS-58 Live Events marker redesign, acceptance: **REJECT** → `build`(designer)

- **Did:** acceptance pass on `designer`'s post-ship marker redesign (`passenger-code c2770541`). Read `passenger-brain/CLAUDE.md`, this file's Current Snapshot/recent worklog, and `BOARD.md`'s T-062 row first. **Got a live visual render — this verdict is not a code-read.** The designer's and `qa`'s simulator interaction block did not reproduce: pre-granting location with `xcrun simctl privacy <udid> grant location-always` **before** first launch means the permission dialog never appears, so the map is reachable without any tap. Worked in a detached `git worktree` at `c277054` with a dedicated simulator and derived-data path; the shared tree was never touched (`EventLayer.swift` clean throughout).
- **Verdict: REJECT.** Requirements 1, 3, 4 and P1 pass. Requirement 2 fails on its purpose clause — the founder asked for a marker "that will let the user know that there is a live event," and the shipped marker can render **completely invisible**.
- **The finding, measured, same camera/zoom/simulator/build-config, marker design the only variable:**

  | build | event fixture position | marker pixels on screen | visible size |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | old marker (`3435d85`) | seeded, at the Florentin Hood centroid | 8,812 | 43.0 × 43.7 pt |
  | **new marker (`c277054`)** | **seeded, same coordinate** | **0** | **not visible at all** |
  | new marker (`c277054`) | shifted ~190 m off the centroid | 2,545 | 17.7 × 17.7 pt |

  Cause: `HoodLayer.swift:96`'s centroid `Annotation` (the "Florentin" name pill, ~16–20pt tall, drawn above `EventLayer`'s annotation) fully covers the new 18pt core. The old 44pt mark extended past the pill in every direction and could not be hidden this way. **Measured:** it fires at `.close` zoom on the exact seeded fixture the team demos with, whenever an event's coordinate falls inside the label pill's footprint. **[ASSUMPTION]** — how often real Tel Aviv events land that close to a Hood centroid is unmeasured; I did not size it, and it should not be reported as if I had. What is not an assumption is that the failure mode exists, is reproducible, and is new to this redesign. Cold-open city-wide zoom is unaffected — Hood labels don't render there, and the marker read cleanly.
- **Verified live, passing — not accepted on code-read:** (a) **micro-animation runs.** `simctl io screenshot` returns a settled frame and showed 8 byte-identical captures, which is a capture artifact, not a dead animation — video at 10fps shows the halo band's mean luminance cycling with minima 16 frames apart, i.e. **1.6 s**, matching the spec exactly. (b) **Reduce Motion is genuinely honoured.** With `ReduceMotionEnabled` set and the device rebooted, the same band is flat across 32 frames (spread 0.7/255, against 6.9 with motion on) and the core still renders at 18pt. (c) Core measures 17.7 × 17.7 pt, contrast ≈ **11.7:1** against the map's light tiles — well past WCAG AA's 3:1 for UI components (`design/design-principles.md` §4). **Size and contrast are not the defect; occlusion is.** (d) Tap target, `accessibilityLabel`, `accessibilityIdentifier` unchanged — confirmed by read, matching `chief-of-staff`'s independent check.
- **Second finding, designer's judgment to weigh, not a hard fail:** the pulse is at the low end of noticeable. Its mean luminance swing over the halo band is ~7/255 (≈2.7%) across the full cycle; peak per-pixel delta between cycle extremes is 164/765. It reads as a soft breath rather than a "live" cue, and it does nothing at all when the core is occluded. The halo is the natural place to fix both — worth revisiting amplitude/extent in the same pass.
- **Explicitly not asking for a revert to 44pt.** Aviran's "too big" stands; smaller and more solid is the right direction and requirement 1 is met. What's missing is a legibility floor. Options are the designer's call: raise `EventLayer` above the centroid annotation in the `MapContent` z-order, give the core a light outline/ring that extends past the label pill, or bump the core modestly (~24–26pt, still far under 44).
- **PRD fixed in this same commit (L-009):** `prds/live-events-overlay/live-events-overlay.md` req 1 gains a marker-legibility bullet stating the rendered consequence ("at least half the marker's drawn area still shows"), plus a Decisions-log row. Every earlier gate passed this redesign because no bullet ever required the marker to be *visible* — "distinguishable from place pins" presumes it renders. Does not re-open reqs 1–5's 2026-08-03 acceptance; the marker shipped then passed this bullet. HTML twin regenerated via `md2html.convert()` on that one file only, not the module's full `FILES` sweep, to avoid touching other sessions' in-flight PRDs (rule 2).
- **Left behind:** (1) **the simulator interaction block has a workaround worth trying at `T-038`/`PAS-29`** — grant location privacy *before* first launch rather than dismissing the dialog after; that was the difference here, and `qa` has burned three passes on it. (2) `simctl io screenshot` cannot capture animation — use `recordVideo` + `ffmpeg` for any motion check. (3) Occlusion between `HoodLayer`'s centroid label and other map annotations has no owner; `PlaceLayer`'s 44pt pins are safe today, so this is only a live problem for whatever shrinks next.
- **Git:** `passenger-brain/prds/live-events-overlay/live-events-overlay.md`, `…/live-events-overlay.html`, `agent-os/PROGRESS.md` (this entry). Explicit paths, `git diff --staged` re-read before commit per rule 2. **BOARD.md and Linear deliberately untouched** — `chief-of-staff` reconciles both once it has this verdict, per its dispatch. Not pushed — Aviran-gated, `CLAUDE.md` rule 9. Hash in the final response.

### 2026-08-04 — designer — T-062/PAS-58: Live Events marker redesign — smaller, solid, micro-pulse

- **Did:** post-ship redesign pass against the founder-direct request recorded at this file's 2026-08-04 L-002 stub ("the icon of the live events is too big. we need something more solid and small with micro animation that will let the user know that there is a live event"). Read `passenger-brain/CLAUDE.md`, `passenger-code/CLAUDE.md`, this file's Current Snapshot/recent worklog, and `BOARD.md`'s T-062 row first, per protocol. Worked against the actual shipped code (`passenger-code/Passenger/Map/EventLayer.swift`), not a fresh mockup — no mockup produced or needed, per the retired pre-build gate not applying here.
- **Change:** replaced the 44×44 fully-filled `RoundedRectangle` + thin `Image(systemName: "sparkles")` glyph with a new `LiveEventMarkerGlyph`: an 18×18 solid rounded-square core plus a 30×30 halo that pulses outward and fades, looping via `.repeatForever`. Halo is capped well inside the marker's own 44×44 tap footprint, so it can't compete with the heatmap's own area/fill channel — the exact guarantee `EventLayer.swift`'s own doc comment already made (§2.3 req 2 bullet 1), unchanged by this pass.
- **Requirement-by-requirement:**
  1. Smaller/more solid — visible mark shrank from filling the full 44pt frame to an 18pt solid core (no thin glyph on top).
  2. Micro-animation communicating "live" without competing with heat's area channel — the pulsing halo, capped at 30pt, well under any heat-polygon scale.
  3. Reduce Motion — `@Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion)` (SwiftUI-native, per the task's own preferred form). When on, the halo view isn't even constructed and no animation starts; core renders solid and static.
  4. Tap target/accessibility — 44×44 `Button` frame, `accessibilityLabel("\(event.name), event, \(event.timeLabel)")`, and `accessibilityIdentifier("eventMarker-\(event.id)")` are all byte-for-byte unchanged; only the drawn content inside the frame changed.
  5. P1 shape reconsideration — kept the rounded-square silhouette (not a diamond/star) rather than `PlaceLayer`'s `Circle`: at 18pt map scale a diamond reads close enough to a small circle to blur the exact place/event greyscale distinction the shape exists for (`design-principles.md` §3, "never rely on color alone"); rounded square stays unambiguous at the smaller size. Considered, documented in the file's own doc comment, not applied.
- **Build verification, honestly reported:** the shared `passenger-code` working tree is heavily dirty with several other sessions' in-flight, non-compiling WIP (a `RoutePreview.swift:30` "`ScenicUnavailable` does not conform to `Error`" failure unrelated to this change, confirmed by building the shared tree first and seeing the failure land elsewhere, not in `EventLayer.swift`). To get an honest signal isolated from that, built in a detached `git worktree` pinned to `HEAD` (`3435d85`) with only this file's diff applied, dedicated `-derivedDataPath`: **BUILD SUCCEEDED**, no warnings on the new code. Installed and launched on a booted `iPhone 17 Pro` simulator; app opens to the map. **Could not get a live on-device screenshot of the marker itself** — the same location-permission-dialog interaction block `qa`'s T-038/PAS-29 round-10/11 passes already hit and documented in this file (taps/pinch gestures on the map not registering, even directly on map content, not just chrome buttons) reproduced here too; not re-investigated, since it's already an open, flagged, pre-existing environment issue, not something this pass caused or could fix. Cleaned up: uninstalled the test build, removed the worktree and its dedicated derived data (disk recovered 4.7Gi → 8.1Gi free).
- **Left behind / open for `product`'s acceptance pass:** (1) no live visual render was captured — acceptance will need either a working simulator interaction path or a device to actually see the pulse; (2) the halo's exact timing (1.6s ease-out loop) and opacity/scale curve (0.45→0, 0.6×→1×) are a first-pass judgment call, not measured against any prior art — flag if it reads too fast/slow/subtle once seen live; (3) the "solid, no icon" choice (dropping `sparkles` entirely rather than swapping to a bolder glyph) rests on `EventLayer.swift`'s own pre-existing reasoning that shape, not the icon, carries the place/event distinction — worth a second look from `product`/Aviran if a fully iconless marker reads as less obviously "an event" than intended.
- **Git:** `passenger-code c2770541` (`Passenger/Map/EventLayer.swift`, explicit path staged). `passenger-brain/agent-os/BOARD.md` (T-062 row updated), `passenger-brain/agent-os/PROGRESS.md` (this entry). ### 2026-08-04 — architect — T-057/PAS-46 Scenic Walk TRD: amendment A3 (runtime camera inset, RouteControls accessibility row)

- **Did:** amended `prds/scenic-walk/TRD.md` in place to resolve `ios-code-reviewer`'s findings **2 and 3** from its trd-review AGREE (`passenger-brain dd68110`) — the two its own review, and my previous T-057 pass, both named as deserving the same doc-only treatment A1/A2 got. Documentation-only, no re-review cycle owed. Read `passenger-brain/CLAUDE.md`, this file's recent worklog, and the TRD in full first; checked `passenger-code/Passenger/Map/ProfileButton.swift` and `SearchButton.swift` directly rather than taking the review note's word for the "every other interactive control" claim — both are literally `.frame(width: 44, height: 44)` with the comment *"Fitts's Law minimum (design-principles.md §2)"* plus an `.accessibilityLabel`, so §9 row 15 is written against the real idiom.
- **A3(a) — the camera bottom inset is measured, never hardcoded.** §4.9 justified the inset with `qa`'s single iPhone 17 measurement (`.medium` sheet at y 415–866). That measurement is the **evidence the inset is needed** and is the wrong thing to ship: a `.medium` detent's height moves with Dynamic Type and with iPad/landscape size classes, and a route fitted against a stale constant lands under the sheet in exactly the configurations least likely to be reviewed. §4.9 now requires the inset to be read from the sheet's **rendered** frame at every fit, names the mechanism in preference order (height published up from the sheet content's `onGeometryChange`/`GeometryReader` to `MapScreen`, which already owns both surfaces — no new plumbing layer; else a `safeAreaInset`-based fit), and states two hard rules: derived from a measured frame every time, and **no device-specific pixel constant anywhere in the fit path**. One stated edge: a resolve completing before first layout fits with **zero** inset and re-fits once on the first height report — the only re-fit this feature permits, and explicitly not a second camera move in the sense §9 row 12 forbids.
- **A3(b) — §9 gained row 15, and row 12 gained the check that actually catches a constant.** Row 12 now runs **twice** — default size and `UICTContentSizeCategoryAccessibilityExtraExtraExtraLarge` — asserting first that the sheet is genuinely taller at the larger size, then that the containment still holds **and the two runs' camera regions are not identical**, which is precisely what a hardcoded inset would produce; plus a grep that fails on a device constant in the fit path, with a positive control. **Row 15** (new, per L-032 — a normative statement with no row is a rule no gate reads) covers `RouteControls`: element count **3** asserted before any ∀, then 44×44 frames; VoiceOver labels that carry duration/distance and, in each of the 6 disabled cases, the §4.10 **reason** — so a VoiceOver user gets what a sighted user reads off the visible line, with `isEnabled == false` asserted alongside rather than instead; and AX5 with no truncation of the duration/distance/`via <Hood>` text, checked on rendered geometry. **Row 15 deliberately does not grep `.lineLimit`** — T-038 §9 row 8(c-ii) already established that `.lineLimit`'s absence is not what prevents truncation; `.fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)` is, and its presence is a supporting fact, not the check.
- **Sections touched:** §4.9, §9 rows 12 and 15 (new), §10 C5/C6/C7/C8, header amendment table (new **A3** row), §12, new decision **D17**.
- **Two of `ios-code-reviewer`'s five findings deliberately left open, and now named in §12 rather than left in a worklog entry:** its finding 1 (the 2.5 s `resolveBudget` is enforced between candidate attempts, not within one, so a single slow-but-not-throttled leg has no forced cutoff) and finding 4 (the camera fit animation doesn't address Reduce Motion). Both are **behaviour** changes, not verification defects, so folding them into a documentation-only amendment would have been the wrong instrument — they stay `ios-developer`'s build-time calls, but they are now written into the document instead of living only in a review comment.

- **The defect, confirmed at source:** `PAS-49` (`passenger-code c1b8bc3`/`5e1f72f`) rewrote `HoodLayer.body` to draw `.foregroundStyle(.clear)` in every stroke branch. `fillColor` — the property §9 row 4 named and the only thing `HoodLayerFillDimTests` asserts — is no longer read by `body`. It still computes correctly, so the suite stays green and proves nothing. `borderColor` (`HoodLayer.swift:165-169`) is the channel that renders and does carry `* dimOpacity` in both branches, with **zero** test coverage anywhere.
- **Amended:** §9 row 4 **(a)/(b)/(f)** retargeted at `borderColor`; §4.10 rewritten to describe the border-only render; new build step **C15**; new decision **D15**; D14's now-superseded 4(a) row annotated in place rather than rewritten; a **third standing rule** added to §9's preamble.
- **Four calls inside the amendment that were not in the QA finding, stated rather than buried.** (1) **Row 4(a) asserts the 0.25 *ratio*, not just "strictly less"** — an inequality passes against a floored or clamped multiplier; the ratio doesn't. (2) **Three fixture conditions that silently invalidate the run if unmet:** `isHovered == false` on all 24 layers (`hoverGlow`'s 1.4 is a second uncontrolled input to the same alpha — it did not exist when v2 was written), at least one Hood per band (`borderColor` clamps at `min(bandStrength × hoverGlow, 1)`, and a single-band fixture cannot tell a correct multiply from a clamped one), and the coverage grep run **first**. (3) **Row 4(f) was wrong in a way the retarget exposes, not created:** a `nil`-band Hood renders a visible neutral `.secondary` hairline, so a check expecting "nothing renders" would **fail a correct implementation**; and under the old fill wording, "every one of the other 23 dims strictly" was actually *false* for any `nil`-band Hood among the 23, since `.clear` dims to `.clear`. The border channel fixes both. (4) **`UIColor(Color.secondary.opacity(x))` is named as the one known fragility** — if it doesn't resolve to a comparable alpha in a unit test, the `nil`-band Hoods are recorded as **BLOCKED or checked rendered**, never passed by omission.
- **§4.10's `nil`-band limit is narrowed, not resolved — flagged to `product`.** Under border-only rendering a matched `nil`-band Hood keeps a **full-strength neutral outline** while the other 23 drop to 0.25, so there is now a positive mark on the match rather than only the absence of dimming elsewhere. The surviving limit is that the mark is **uncoloured**, not that it is absent. `product` should confirm that reading rather than inherit v2's wording.
- **Why `fillColor` is not deleted, since it is the obvious fix:** deletion is a production change to a shipped file, on a task sitting at `qa`, to fix a *verification* defect — the two shouldn't be bundled, and the design question below should settle first. Named in D15 rather than quietly skipped. **C15 changes no production behaviour**: it makes `borderColor` internal (the same trade `fillColor` already made and documented) and rewrites the suite.
- **The general lesson, written into §9 as a standing rule.** This is L-009's **third** occurrence on this one requirement (T-046/LOC-104, T-053/PAS-43, now this) and the **second on row 4**. The first two were wrong-*layer* checks. This one is different and worse: the check was written at the right layer and **became** wrong when the layer moved underneath it. So the new rule is not "check the render" — v2 already said that — it is: **name the channel the view draws, and anchor every colour/opacity row on a positive coverage grep, so losing that channel's tests fails the row instead of silently passing it.** A verification row is a claim about the code and it decays.
- **Drift found, not mine to fix, and it has no row yet:** `design/map-rendering-spec.md` §2 still states *"heat is always the area/fill treatment"* — flatly contradicted by the shipped border-only render — and `PAS-49`'s change is recorded in **no** PRD, TRD or design doc anywhere in `passenger-brain`. **Filed as `BOARD.md` row T-060**, owner `designer` (that file's owner), `product` if it turns out to be scope rather than documentation — a row, not a worklog line, per rule 5 / L-026. **Worth recording how close that came to not happening:** when I started, `BOARD.md` carried another session's uncommitted edits and rule 2 would have blocked me from staging it — leaving rule 5's own remedy unavailable, since the file I was told to file the finding *on* was the blocked one. Two commits (`df88b91`, `b859f56`) landed mid-session and cleaned it, so I re-checked `git status` at commit time instead of trusting the reading from the start of my turn, and the row exists. If `BOARD.md` had still been dirty this would have been a worklog line and nothing more, which is exactly the failure L-026 describes. **[ASSUMPTION]**, stated in D15 and in T-060: `PAS-49` was an intended design fix, not a regression — its commit message reads as deliberate. If T-060 concludes otherwise, §9 row 4 and C15 revert with it.
- **Evidence:** no code written or run — design-document amendment. `HoodLayer.swift` read in full (the `body` branches, `fillColor`'s doc comment, `borderColor`, `hoverGlow`, `strokeWidth`). `grep` over `design/`, `prds/` and `strategy/decisions.md` for any record of the border-only decision → **0 hits**, which is the basis of the drift finding above. Table integrity re-checked after editing.

(2) `qa`'s row 4(a) live before/after comparison is still owed once the machine has headroom, and should now be run against **borders**, not fills. No background location, no new location purpose beyond what's already declared for the existing permission flow, no ATT surface (no IDFA/tracking of any kind). §3.3's privacy contract (never receives a `CLLocation`, no persistence, no logging, memo keyed on `Place.id` alone, enforced by §9 row 11's greps with a positive control) is the strongest part of the document.
- **Five findings posted to `PAS-46`, none blocking `build`:** (1) §4.6's 2.5s `resolveBudget` is checked *between* candidate attempts in the flow (§5), not enforced *within* one — no per-leg timeout/race wraps an individual `MKDirections` call, so a single slow (not throttled) response has no forced cutoff and PRD req 7's 3s is a soft target rather than the "structural" guarantee §4.6 claims; recommend a timeout race in `WalkingRouteProvider`/`RoutePreviewModel.resolve`. (2) §4.9's camera bottom-inset is justified by a single hardcoded iPhone 17 QA measurement (y 415–866) — TRD should make explicit that C6 reads the actual rendered sheet frame at runtime, not a device-specific constant, since Dynamic Type and iPad size classes both change sheet height. (3) §9 has no row for RouteControls' 44×44 touch targets, VoiceOver labels, or Dynamic Type, unlike every other interactive control in this codebase (`ProfileButton`, `SearchButton`) — worth an explicit accessibility-label check given the controls carry duration/distance/`via <Hood>` text. (4) The one-time camera fit animation (§4.9) doesn't address Reduce Motion. (5) D3 (`MKMapItem.forCurrentLocation()` on iOS 26) is correctly flagged as trd-review's #1 item by the TRD itself — agreed it should be confirmed at build (C3) rather than block review now, since the named fallback preserves the privacy contract either way.
- **Verdict: AGREE.** C1–C9 is architecturally sound, privacy-correct, and low App Store risk; the five findings are additions/clarifications for `ios-developer` to carry into `build` (1/2/4 into C3/C6, 3 into C5/C8's test pass, 5 already TRD's own open question), not grounds to send the TRD back.
- **Left behind:** `chief-of-staff` should confirm the `ios-developer` half of this review pair has also landed before moving T-057's client surface to `build`. The five findings are non-blocking notes, not tracked as separate follow-up tickets — they belong in the `ios-developer`'s build-time judgment calls per the TRD's own §12 pattern.

### 2026-08-04 — architect — T-057/`PAS-46` Scenic Walk (lighter version): TRD written, `trd` → `trd-review`

- **Did:** wrote `prds/scenic-walk/TRD.md` from the approved PRD (Draft v1, `product`, 2026-08-04) against decision #44. Updated T-057's `BOARD.md` row to `trd-review`. Grilling gate **skipped deliberately** — dispatched autonomously with no interactive founder in the loop (`architect.md`: never answer your own questions); every call that would have gone to Aviran is carried as **[ASSUMPTION]** and listed in TRD §12.
- **Surface split (what chief-of-staff needs to dispatch on):** **[iOS] for steps C1–C9, [Algo/Data] for step A1, and no [Backend] step at all** — no schema, no column, no RLS, no endpoint, no Passenger backend call (§3.1). Confirmed against the code, not inherited from the dispatch brief. `code-reviewer` is still on the review list because A1 re-runs `build_hoods.py`, which emits a SQL seed migration alongside the iOS bundle. **Two review pairs: `ios-developer` + `ios-code-reviewer`; `data-engineer` + `code-reviewer`.**
- **The PRD's four open technical questions, all resolved (§1.1):** (1) **MapKit `MKDirections`, chained — Google Directions rejected** (§6, D1/D2). Google costs money and needs an account, both Aviran-gated; it puts an API key in the client; and its platform terms restrict displaying Directions content on a non-Google map — that last point tagged **[ASSUMPTION]**, recalled rather than re-read this session, and deliberately not load-bearing since the first two decide it alone. One waypoint in V1, not two = 2 chained legs concatenated with a 5 m seam dedup. (2) **Request volume: ≤3 `MKDirections` calls per modal open, 5 worst case, 0 per route-control tap, 0 on re-open within a 5-minute session memo** keyed on `Place.id` alone (§4.7). (3) **The hand-off cannot carry waypoints** — no public API puts an intermediate stop into Apple Maps — so req 5's disclosure is unconditional and pre-tap, never an alert after (§4.8). (4) **Req 8's fixture is Hoods-only** (§3.4, D13).
- **Three things the PRD did not know, each found by reading `passenger-code/` rather than assuming:**
  - **`LocationStore` holds no coordinates by design** — its own doc comment reads "Authorization status only — no coordinates, ever." A route needs an origin. Resolved by using `MKMapItem.forCurrentLocation()` as the `MKDirections` source, so the app never receives or stores a `CLLocation`; route geometry is in-memory for one modal presentation only, no cache key contains a coordinate, and `Routing/` carries no logging (§3.3, §4.3, D3). Whether that API survived the iOS 26 SDK's `MKMapItem` deprecations is `trd-review` question 1, with a fallback path named so the build isn't blocked either way.
  - **The PRD's ranking key is degenerate on today's data.** It proposes ranking candidate Hoods by curated-place count. Counted directly: `places-tel-aviv.json` holds **9 places in exactly 3 Hoods** (`florentin`, `kerem-hateimanim`, `neve-tzedek`, 3 each) and **not one of them is `false`-flagged** — the key is 0 for every eligible candidate. Kept as the primary sort for real data, plus a second non-degenerate key (waypoint distance off-route) and a `Hood.centroid` waypoint fallback for a Hood with no curated place (§4.5, D6).
  - **"Draws its polyline inside the modal's own space" resolves to the main map behind the sheet, not a mini-map** — argued from the PRD's own next bullet, which asks that a route line be distinguishable from a Hood's tourist-trap outline at neighborhood zoom, and Hood outlines are drawn by `HoodLayer` on the main map and nowhere else (§1.2, §4.9, D9). Still tagged **[ASSUMPTION]** and raised as `trd-review` question 2: if `product` meant a map *inside* the modal, §4.9, two §9 rows and step C6 all change.
- **The four PRD [ASSUMPTION]s, adjudicated rather than passed through:** waypoint heuristic **refined** — the corridor is derived from the **fast route's own polyline**, not the straight A→B line, buffer 800 m. Measured, not guessed: on an Old North → Neve Tzedek corridor a 500 m straight-line buffer catches only Hoods the route already runs through (3 m, 5 m, 25 m), with the first genuinely off-route Hood at 433 m — 500 m would empty the candidate set by construction. Detour bounds **ratified as proposed** (1.5× AND +15 min, which is a `min`, not two independent tests) **plus a new 5-minute floor, mine, [ASSUMPTION]**. The 3 s budget **ratified and made structural** — a 2.5 s wall-clock resolve budget plus a 2-candidate attempt cap, so the bound is enforced by the loop rather than hoped for. Modal-only entry point **ratified**.
- **§9 carries 12 verification rows — the 8 P0s plus 4 normative rules pulled out of §2–§5** (the corridor filters, the request-volume caps, the no-location-persisted contract, the camera fit), per L-032. Every negative-existence check carries a named positive control; every ∀ is preceded by an exact count; every visibility row asserts rendered frames rather than `.exists`. **Req 4's "identical polyline" rule is implemented as a divergence test** (≥100 m contiguous run outside the fast route's 25 m corridor), because MapKit returns different point counts for the same path — a byte-equality check would never fire, and the requirement would have passed by never being exercised (D8).
- **Fixture (req 8), specified as constraints plus a computed proposal:** ≥3 mutually non-adjacent `false`-flagged Hoods, non-adjacency defined falsifiably (no vertex pair within 50 m, centroids ≥800 m apart), on one documented demo corridor, provisional-marked per the `florentin` blurb precedent, asserted against `Bundle.main` in the `PassportBundleInvariantTests` style, and verified by re-running the generator to a scratch path and diffing — the only check that proves no hand-edit survived (L-024). Geometric proposal computed from the committed source polygons: `old-north`, `montefiore`, `shapira`; min vertex separations 1136/2865/428 m, centroid separations 2830/4454/2290 m; demo corridor origin `32.0945, 34.7981` (Bavli) → `florentin-anna-loulou-bar`, with `montefiore` 715 m and `shapira` 1102 m off that line, both inside the 250–1200 m waypoint band. **The substance is `data-engineer`'s and Aviran's, not mine** — whether those three neighbourhoods *are* not tourist-heavy is a data claim this TRD has no standing to make, and straight-line geometry must be re-measured against a real `MKDirections` walking route before the fixture is committed.
- **Deliberately did NOT touch `places-tel-aviv.json`** (D13). Adding a curated place to a `false`-flagged Hood would exercise the primary waypoint path on device, but it would also change the shipped seed that `SearchShippedSeedTests` and `search-quick-filters/TRD.md` §9 row 3 assert **exact arrays** against — real breakage in another feature's passing tests, for coverage a pure unit fixture gives for free. Consequence stated in the TRD rather than hidden: the on-device Phase-1 demo exercises the centroid fallback, and §9 row 8(d) says so.
- **Left behind — one new risk, for Aviran/`product`, that the architecture cannot solve (§8 R1):** "not flagged tourist-heavy" is being used as a proxy for "worth walking through," and it is not one. Decision #37 retired the graduated tag, so `isTouristTrap == false` is the entire basis of the recommendation in V1 — nothing in this design would stop a `false` flag on, say, the old central-bus-station area from becoming a recommended detour. Either accept that, or add a second gate before real Phase-2 data drives it.
- **Also left behind, unchanged from the PRD and still Aviran's:** `strategy/passenger-strategy.md`'s V1-scope navigation bullet still describes decision #32's weighted per-segment routing and now contradicts what this TRD specifies. Aviran-gated file — **reported, not edited** (`CLAUDE.md` rule 8). And req 5's disclosed gap: the scenic detour cannot survive the hand-off, so a user can preview one walk and take another; §4.8 makes the disclosure unconditional and pre-tap, but whether that trade is acceptable is his call. One question for `code-reviewer` rather than Aviran: `006_` and `007_hoods_tel_aviv_data.sql` both already seed the same table and neither is applied — the TRD recommends regenerating `007` in place rather than adding an `008`, as a recommendation, not a ruling.

One full `xcodebuild test` run's `PassengerUITests-Runner` hit "test runner timed out while preparing to run tests" on first attempt (environment, not code — retry succeeded 19/19 clean). Manual taps stayed unreliable even after load dropped to single digits, while XCUITest's own synthesized touches (in-process via the linked XCTest framework, not external simulator touch injection) worked reliably throughout every attempt.
- **Response to the environment issue:** rather than force a BLOCKED verdict on the four briefed items, wrote a live UI test (`PassengerUITests/PlacesListInteractionTests.swift`, `passenger-code 92561a7`, 6 tests) that exercises exactly what a manual click-through would have — this closes the "live, not code read" gap the reviewer asked for and leaves permanent regression coverage behind instead of a one-off. All 6 pass against current `main` (`0e3b3dc`+this commit): closed-badge row (`neve-nachum-gutman-museum`) opens the detail modal with `Directions` enabled (never blocked); all three dismissal paths (✕, scrim tap, drag past the 80pt threshold) each return to an unchanged map; D8 direction 1 (opening Places over an open Heat modal replaces it) confirmed live; D8 direction 2 (dismissing a stacked place modal reveals the list unchanged, then leaving `.places` for Heat closes it) confirmed live, after adjusting the test to a physically reachable path — see finding below.

### 2026-08-03 — architect — T-055 time-slider TRD §9: the z5 layout rule finally gets a verification row (TRD v4)

- **Did:** `prds/time-slider/TRD.md` → **v4**. One substantive addition — **§9 row 5b**, the check §2.3's z5 layering rule never had. Plus a §9 preamble carrying three standing rules, a matching §10 risk row, and the v4 changelog block. **§2.3's z5 rule itself is unchanged** — it was correct as written and the build deviated from it; this fixes the *gate*, not the *design*.
- **The row, and why it is shaped this way.** Observable is the **rendered frames**, never the padding constant: with the heat modal presented, `HeatModalCard.frame` and `MapNavRow.frame` must not intersect, separated by a fixed gap (≥8pt — an **[ASSUMPTION]** floor, since §2.3 requires the distance be *fixed and non-zero* and names no number; the constant is `ios-developer`'s at build, and if a different fixed distance is chosen the floor moves to it). Asserted **separately for each of the three readout elements** — offset numeral, clock label, "next day" pill — because the card can clear the nav row while a pill drawn at its edge does not. Run **twice**: default text size *and* AX5, since the card is sized-to-content and a default-size gap proves nothing about the AX5 one. Plus `card.frame.maxY <` safe-area bottom, so `bottom: 0` is falsified by name rather than inferred from the gap. Non-empty frames are asserted **first**, with values recorded — two frames that never rendered do not intersect either, which is exactly how this row could pass while the requirement fails. Layer is a **rendered UI test**, explicitly not unit, not source review, not `exists` — all three passed this build. Steps **C2, C5**: C2 wires the nav row in at z7, C5 builds the card, and neither alone can check a relationship it owns half of.
- **One thing I was careful not to claim.** The positive control (the pill's `label` reads `"next day"` in full) **does not detect the occlusion** and the row says so in as many words. `XCUIElement.label` returns the whole string for a fully covered `Text` — that is precisely why F1 survived `qa`. Its only job is to prove the elements rendered at all, so the geometric assertions are claims about something. A row that leaned on the label check would have reproduced the bug it exists to catch.
- **Standing rules — lifted locally, deliberately not workspace-wide.** §9's preamble now states the two rules T-053 added to the `search-quick-filters` TRD (no pass condition satisfiable over an empty set; every negative-existence check needs a positive control) plus a third for this feature's shape (rendered-result rows are run on a rendered app; blocked → **BLOCKED**, reported as unrun). Restated rather than cross-referenced because `qa` reads this table standalone. **Rows 1–7 were not re-audited against them in this pass** and the preamble says so — a partial audit silently presented as a full one is the same class of problem as a vacuous pass condition. Whether these belong in `architect.md` as fleet-wide rules is `retrospective`'s call; I did not make it here.
- **Documentation-only — this blocks nothing.** No code, no schema, no contract, no decision reopened, no build step changed. **No `trd-review` re-run is owed and this does not gate `ios-developer`'s in-flight T-032 rebuild**, whose correctness was already fully specified by §2.3 z5 and PRD v9's req 5 bullet, both predating v4. Same shape as T-053's §9 amendment.
- **Third instance of one failure shape (L-009):** T-046, then T-053/`PAS-43`, now this. All three are a real rule stated somewhere no gate reads.
- **HTML twins regenerated, and one of them is not mine — disclosed rather than flagged.** Ran `prds/md2html.py` (17 files written, 3 changed on disk): `time-slider/TRD.html` (mine, from this v4), `time-slider/time-slider.html` (stale since `product`'s PRD v9 at `73210bc`), `search-quick-filters/search-quick-filters.html` (stale since T-053's amendment, source committed at `9c827af`). Both non-mine files are mechanical renders of **already-committed** markdown, so no other session's in-flight work is swept in. Staged and named in the commit message per `bfd0c7e`'s precedent — `time-slider/TRD.html` is the exact artifact L-026/L-027 are about, and a fourth "flagged for whoever owns it" was not an option.
- **Left behind:** (1) **No Linear issue for T-055** — deliberately not invented, `chief-of-staff` creates it (T-053 labelled itself `PAS-41`, which was a different task, and three references needed correcting after the fact). (2) The 8pt gap floor is an **[ASSUMPTION]**; if `ios-developer` picks a different fixed distance at the rebuild, row 5b's number moves with it — what may not move is that the gap is fixed, positive, and asserted. (3) Row 5b binds this TRD only. The four sibling z5 surfaces (`PassportSurface`, `PlacesListOverlay`, `SearchOverlay`) share the anchoring pattern and are **T-054**'s, named in the new §10 row so nobody reads 5b as covering them. (4) Rows 1–7 unaudited against the three standing rules, above.

- **Did:** the `acceptance` step on T-032/PAS-15, arriving from `qa`'s PASS WITH MINORS. Read `passenger-brain/CLAUDE.md`, `BOARD.md`'s T-032 row in full (both tables), this file's recent worklog (`qa`'s T-032 entry, `ios-code-reviewer`'s T-032 code-review, my own T-034/T-035/T-036 pass for method), the PRD (v8) and `TRD.md` v3, and `TEST-PLAN.md`'s 27 cases. A place's relevance changes by the hour; the map knows that. Unchanged."* Nothing social, no onboarding, no Phase 2/3 hooks. The gesture change (v2/v3) doesn't need a new citation: the line names the control and its range, not how a finger reaches it.

**Verdict: REJECT → `build`. Two blocking findings, both rendered-only, both invisible to every gate that ran before this one.**

- **F1 (blocking) — the nav row draws on top of the modal's readout, at the DEFAULT text size.** Not an accessibility edge case: `MapNavRow`'s Heat and Search buttons sit on the "next day" flag in `HourReadout`, which renders as "…t day". At +12h/11:00 that matters — "+12h 11:00" without the flag reads as 11:00 *today*, so the readout can state the wrong hour. **This is a straight deviation from the TRD's own §2.3 z-table**, which specifies z5 as *"anchored a fixed distance above the nav row, sized to content — never `bottom: 0`"*. The build ships `HeatModalCard` as `ZStack(alignment: .bottom)` + `.padding(.bottom, 8)`, while `MapScreen.swift` places `MapNavRow` in `.overlay(alignment: .bottom).padding(.bottom, 96)` — so the card grows upward straight through the nav row's band. The z7 row's other half ("never covered") is satisfied; the z5 half is not, and the pair only works together.
- **F2 (blocking) — the readout is not legible at the largest supported Dynamic Type size.** At AX5 the offset label wraps mid-token ("+12" on one line, "h" on the next) and the "next day" pill breaks across two lines inside a capsule that no longer contains it. `grep` for `dynamicTypeSize` across `Passenger/` returns nothing, so AX5 genuinely is "the largest supported size" — there is no cap making this out of scope. Re-check F2 after F1's fix: a correctly anchored card may reflow, but the mid-token wrap is a layout failure independent of the occlusion.
- **Why no earlier gate caught either.** `code-review` reviewed against the TRD end-to-end but never rendered the app. `qa`'s C16 (the AX5 row) was one of the 11 the disk exhaustion blocked. And nothing anywhere covered F1: §2.3's z-table is stated as architecture and **never became a §9 verification row or a TEST-PLAN case**, so no gate had a rendered pass condition to fail. Element-existence assertions cannot see this — `XCUIElement.exists` is `true` for a fully occluded label — and neither can a source read. **Spec defect as much as a build defect (L-009): req 5 gains the missing rendered bullet in the same commit as this verdict**, stated as what the user sees, not as a stored value. PRD → **Draft v9**, status deliberately *not* flipped to Accepted.

**The 11 BLOCKED rows, re-run live — `qa`'s environment blocker is gone and both reviewer asks are now closed.**

- **Environment:** `df -h /` showed 45Gi free, `ps aux` zero concurrent `xcodebuild`, one booted simulator — the wall three sessions hit today is down. Ran on a **clean detached `git worktree` at `passenger-code d537ca5`**, deliberately not the shared working tree, which held T-051/T-052 WIP in `MapScreen.swift`/`EventDetailModal.swift` — testing T-032 against another task's uncommitted edits would not have been evidence about T-032. Dedicated simulator, own `derivedDataPath`.
- **C21 (reviewer's ask #1) — PASS, live.** `EdgeHourZoneInteractionTests` executed 3/3 clean in 64.2s, zero failures, including `testInBandVerticalDragMovesTheHourAndLeavesTheCameraUntouched`: camera byte-identical across two real consecutive in-band drags while `selectedHour` moved. `qa` re-verified this test's *construction*; this pass re-verified its *result*.
- **C26 (reviewer's ask #2) — PASS, live.** No session on record had ever performed the rendered rotation check. Wrote a throwaway probe: rotate to `.landscapeLeft`, perform an in-band vertical edge drag → hour unchanged at `0`; rotate back to portrait, perform the **identical** drag → hour moves. The negative control is the whole point — without it, "nothing happened in landscape" is equally consistent with a drag that simply missed.
- **C5 — PASS, live.** `HeatRepaintPerformanceTests` measured `HourRepaint` at **average 0.004s**, values `[0.0043, 0.0056, 0.0039, 0.0036, 0.0025]`, against req 2's 400ms budget. Two orders of magnitude of headroom, as the "no fetch on an hour change" architecture predicted.
- **C6 — PASS, closed by probe.** The button-path camera check `qa` logged as a minor gap: swept the slider 0→12, camera dump identical before/mid/after. **The gap is now a missing test, not a missing answer** — the shipped suite still has no such case.
- **C22–C25 — resolved by construction, not blocked.** The four rows split on sheet *detent*, and there is no detent-sensitive code path to split on: `EdgeAvailability.liveEdges` takes no detent argument, and `edgeLayer(for:)` removes `EdgeHourZone` from the hierarchy whenever `isAnySheetPresented`. `.medium` and `.large` cannot differ. `testEdgeZoneIsInertWhileAHoodSheetIsPresented` also ran clean live.
- **C13 — PASS (structural).** Both paths draw the "now" mark as `diamond.fill` against hairline `Rectangle` (slider) / 3pt `Circle` (edge track) stops — shape-distinct, so greyscale is irrelevant.
- **400/400 unit tests green** (71 suites, Swift Testing) on the same worktree.
- **Still open, non-blocking:** C14 (no live VoiceOver session — unchanged from `qa`'s position); C20 — confirmed the intended control case was never written, `EdgeHourZoneInteractionTests.mapCenterX` is declared with a comment naming the "pan starts outside the band" case and is referenced by no test in the file.
- **One thing I checked and did NOT count as a finding.** Req 6's button-path bullet says the slider's frame is "≥44pt **on the drag axis**". Measured live: the drawn/hit-testable frame is 354×**31pt**, and a horizontal drag 20pt above its centre — inside the 44pt band `.frame(minHeight: 44)` claims, outside the drawn control — does not move the hour, while the identical drag through the centre moves it 0→12. So the layout container is 44pt and the *touch target* is 31pt. **The bullet still passes as written**, because Q5 (v4) confirmed the button control stays horizontal, making the drag axis the 354pt one. The bullet measures the axis that cannot fail and leaves the acquisition axis unspecified — but 31pt is Apple's own stock `Slider` height, and holding it to 44pt means abandoning the native control, which req 6's VoiceOver bullet and req 6's platform-drawn rail exemption both depend on. That is a scope call (the same shape as Q7, which Aviran ratified), not a `product` call, and not something to smuggle in under a REJECT. **Not raised as a finding, not fixed silently — flagged here so it is on record**, and worth Aviran's ruling if he wants it, separately from this rejection.
- **Cross-task finding, filed rather than folded in:** all four z5 surfaces share the anchoring pattern F1 exposes — `PassportSurface`, `PlacesListOverlay` (both `.padding(.bottom, 8)`) and `SearchOverlay` (`.padding(.bottom, 4)`) all sit under the same 96pt-high floating nav row. Confirmed by source read, **not** by rendering them. Filed as **T-054** with `ios-developer` as owner, per `CLAUDE.md` rule 5 — a defect I find but don't own gets a board row, not a worklog line. Deliberately not folded into T-032's fix: those are three other PRDs' surfaces, two of them already accepted.
- **What `ios-developer` needs to fix, numbered:** (1) anchor `HeatModalCard` a fixed distance above `MapNavRow` per TRD §2.3 z5, so the two never share pixels — not by hiding the nav row, which z7 forbids; (2) make the readout row survive AX5 without wrapping mid-token or breaking the pill. `architect` owes §9 a verification row for the z5 layout rule, which is what let this through.
- **Left behind:** (1) T-054, above. (2) Two cheap tests the shipped suite lacks and this pass proved are writable — a rotation check (C26) and a button-path camera check (C6); probes were throwaway and are not committed to `passenger-code`. (3) C14's live VoiceOver run and C20's control case, both still open and both non-blocking. (4) The 44pt/31pt touch-target question above, for Aviran if he wants it. (5) T-050 is still blocked on this task's C5 — that measurement now exists (4ms), so T-050's re-verification half is unblocked the moment T-032 lands.

- **Did:** first review of `.github/workflows/ios-build.yml` (new file, 33 lines), the build-only GitHub Actions gate `ios-developer` added at `passenger-code 2e8dc53`. No PRD/TRD exists for this task (it's infra, not a feature) — TRD-conformance pass N/A. No UI/HIG/Liquid Glass surface touched — those passes N/A. `/vibe-security` pass: clean, no secrets/keys/tokens in the file, no auth/payment/location code touched.
- **Verified against the live project rather than trusting the commit message:** `xcodebuild -list -project Passenger.xcodeproj` confirms `Passenger` is the project's one and only scheme, matching the workflow's `-scheme Passenger`. `grep -c XCRemoteSwiftPackageReference Passenger.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` → `0` — no remote SPM packages, so the build needs no network dependency resolution beyond `actions/checkout@v4`, removing a whole class of CI flakiness. `SupabaseConfig.plist` is gitignored and referenced only at runtime in `AppConfig.swift`/`BuildPhase.swift` (`grep -rn SupabaseConfig Passenger/`) — its absence in a fresh CI checkout cannot break `xcodebuild build`, since the workflow only compiles, never runs the app.
- **`xcode-version: latest-stable` vs. pinning (the ios-developer's flagged [ASSUMPTION]) — checked, and it's the right call, not just a defensible one.** `project.pbxproj` shows `IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = 26.0`, `SWIFT_VERSION = 6.0`, `SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY = complete` on both build configs — this project targets iOS 26 exclusively, no backward-compat path (matches the fleet's standing "no `if #available`" rule elsewhere). Pinning to an arbitrary specific Xcode number risks landing on one that predates the iOS 26 SDK and hard-failing every run for a reason unrelated to the code being tested; `latest-stable` is the only choice that tracks the SDK the project actually requires. The one residual, unverifiable-from-here risk: whether the `macos-15` runner's current `latest-stable` Xcode already ships the iOS 26 SDK — that's the same "first real push is the actual test" gap `ios-developer` already disclosed in `ONBOARDING.md`, not a defect in this YAML.
- **Build command and destination:** `xcodebuild build -project Passenger.xcodeproj -scheme Passenger -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` is correct for a build-only gate. `generic/platform=iOS Simulator` avoids depending on any specific simulator runtime/device being preinstalled on the runner image — the right choice given the job never launches or tests the app. `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` is required and correctly scoped, since there's no Apple Developer account yet (`ACCOUNTS-AND-COSTS.md`). Trigger scope (`push`/`pull_request` to `main` only) matches the ticket's stated goal of a green build gate, nothing more.
- **Non-blocking minors:** no `timeout-minutes` on the job (GitHub's default is a 6-hour ceiling on hosted runners — cheap insurance against a hung build silently burning Actions minutes); no `concurrency` group to auto-cancel a superseded run on rapid successive pushes; no DerivedData/build caching (low-value here specifically, since there's no SPM network fetch to cache around, but would still speed up repeat builds later). None of these block a first, minimal, "build gate only" gate — worth picking up if/when this workflow grows (e.g. once tests get folded in).
- **Noted, not re-litigated:** the `architect` entry immediately above this one (T-053/`PAS-41` search-quick-filters TRD) already flags that its own Linear ID and this task's Linear ID collide — one of the two is mislabelled. Already surfaced there as `chief-of-staff`'s to resolve in Linear; not re-flagged as a new finding here, just cross-referenced so it isn't lost between the two entries.
- **Verdict: APPROVE.** No blocking findings, no minors that need a fix before this ships. Small, correct, low-risk mechanical change — reviewed to that bar, not padded with invented risk. Moving to `qa`, briefed that there is nothing to behaviorally test here beyond watching the first real Actions run go green once Aviran pushes — the actual open item is the same one `ios-developer` already named: no live GitHub Actions run has been observed yet from any session.

### 2026-08-03 — product — T-038/PAS-29 acceptance pass: **REJECT** — req 4's dim emphasises nothing at the app's own cold-open zoom, and no test anywhere asserts a layer's dim

- **Did:** acceptance pass on T-038 (Search & quick filters) against `prds/search-quick-filters/search-quick-filters.md` and `TRD.md` v1, dispatched after `ios-code-reviewer` APPROVE WITH MINORS and `qa` PASS. Read `BOARD.md`'s two T-038 rows and the `qa` entry below before starting. **Re-derived all eight P0s from `passenger-code` source directly**, per this workspace's standing acceptance discipline — not a re-read of the two upstream verdicts.
  - **Commit tested:** `passenger-code 3d8e3b8`. The brief's "confirmed unchanged by `beb3f02`" was already stale on arrival — `passenger-code 2267090` (`qa`'s own new tests) and `passenger-code 198b082` (T-032's time-slider build) have since landed, and **198b082 rewrites `MapScreen.swift` (+264/−) and `MapNavRow.swift`**, both search-carrying files. Re-derived against current `main` as well as the pinned commit; the search wiring survived T-032 intact (`SearchOverlay` at z5, z3 tap-catcher at `MapScreen.swift:332`, `MapNavRow` search button, `isDimmed` on both layers all present and correct after the merge). No T-032 regression on T-038. Worth stating because a pinned-hash brief plus a fast-moving `main` is how a verdict ends up describing a tree nobody is running.
  1. **Seven of eight P0s hold**, each re-derived rather than accepted: req 1 (one door — `openSearch`/`dismissSearch`/`handlePresentedSurfaceChange` read directly, `grep` for `fullScreenCover|NavigationStack|NavigationLink` over `Search/`+`SearchSheet/` → 0); req 2 (three match kinds — `SearchQuery.run`'s five rules read line by line, visible `Text("Search")` label distinct from the `TextField` prompt); req 3 (two chips, one call site, `.fresh == .all`, checkmark-not-colour selected state); req 5 (routing — both branches call the same `router.openPlace`/`openHood` a pin or polygon tap makes; exactly two real `.sheet(isPresented:` sites app-wide, the other two `grep` hits being `DetailRouter`'s own doc comments); req 6 (four states present; `grep` for `CoreLocation|LocationStore|CLLocation` → 0, so location-denied is structurally a no-op); req 7 (session lives on `MapScreen` as `@State` and `handlePresentedSurfaceChange` takes no `session` parameter — an interruption *cannot* clear it, Poka-Yoke rather than a tested behaviour; all four manual-dismiss paths verified by call site to route through the one `dismissSearch`); req 8 partially — 44pt frames and both pinned VoiceOver strings are real and correct.
  2. **F1 — BLOCKING, PRD req 4 bullet 1. Two compounding halves; together, opening search and typing a match changes nothing a user can see.**
     - **F1a — the Hood dim never reaches the heat fill.** `HoodLayer.dimOpacity` is applied to the polygon's *stroke* (`.opacity(0.35 * dimOpacity)` / `Color("Flag").opacity(dimOpacity)`) and to `annotationContent`, but `MapPolygon.foregroundStyle(fillColor)` is left untouched in all three `effectiveStroke` branches, and `HeatPalette.fill(for:)` returns `hue.opacity(opacity(for: band))` — a fixed per-band alpha with no dim factor. So a non-matching Hood renders its **full-strength heat fill** while search is open. The fill is the dominant visual and the channel req 4 bullet 1 is actually about; what dims is a 0.5pt hairline and a label that is invisible at city-wide zoom anyway. The file's own doc comments assert the opposite **twice** — *"`true` multiplies every visible element's opacity by 0.25"* and *"the one multiplier every visible element in this layer applies"* — so this reads as intended behaviour that was never wired, not a deliberate scoping call.
     - **F1b — a place-only match has no pin to emphasise at the zoom the app opens at.** `MapScreen.swift:244` gates the `PlaceLayer` `ForEach` on `showsNames`, i.e. `zoomTier == .close`, i.e. latitude span **< 0.06**. The shipped cold-open camera is `Self.telAvivCityWide`, span **0.14** → `.cityWide` → **no place pin is constructed at all**. `SearchDim.emphasis` returns `(places: {ids}, hoods: [])` for such a match, so no Hood is emphasised either.
     - **Rendered result at cold open, F1a + F1b together:** heat fills unchanged, hairline strokes marginally fainter, no pins. The map is visually indistinguishable from before the search. Reproduce in ~15 seconds: cold open → search → type `"suzan"` (2 place results, 0 Hood results, both confirmed by `SearchShippedSeedTests`). **Surface:** F1a at every zoom and every query; F1b at every zoom with span ≥ 0.06 (`.cityWide` **and** `.neighborhood`) — the app's opening state for everyone and the *permanent* state for a user who denies location, which PRD req 6 bullet 5 explicitly supports. Not a corner case; it is the primary path for the most common query type.
     - **Correction, disclosed rather than quietly rewritten.** The first version of this entry (`passenger-brain 8545d2b`) described F1 as *"every Hood polygon/stroke/annotation at 0.25 opacity, zero pins, nothing bright."* That was **wrong** — it took `dimOpacity`'s doc comment at its word instead of tracing `fillColor` through `HeatPalette`. The verdict does not change and the requirement still fails, but the mechanism is close to the inverse of what was first written, and F1a is the larger half of the defect. Caught on this agent's own critic pass before delivery (`CLAUDE.md`'s writing rules), corrected in this entry's follow-up commit (hash in the Git line below). Worth recording as its own small lesson: I rejected this build for asserting a passed value instead of a rendered one, and then made the same class of mistake in the rejection by trusting a doc comment instead of the render path.
  3. **Why five gates passed it, and the fix that outlives this task (L-009).** TRD §9 row 4(a)'s pass condition is *"that place's id and that Hood's id are the only members; every other `PlaceLayer`/`HoodLayer` receives `isDimmed == true`"* — every clause of which is **true in the failing case**. It asserts the value handed to a layer, never what the layer draws. And it was never implemented anyway: `grep -rn "isDimmed" PassengerTests/ PassengerUITests/` returns **0**, and `grep` for `showsNames|zoomTier|cityWide` across all five search test files returns **0**. So the requirement had no falsifiable check at any layer, and `SearchDimTests` (green, 3 cases) tests set membership on the pure function while the composition that breaks sits in `MapScreen`. Per L-006/L-009 I wrote the missing criteria into the PRD **in this same commit**, stated as the rendered consequence: req 4 gains *"whenever results show, at least one map element renders undimmed — at every zoom the map can be at, including the cold-open zoom"*, and req 8 gains the chip case. Both labelled as added at acceptance with the reason.
  4. **F2 — non-blocking, fold into the same fix pass, PRD req 8 bullet 3.** `CategoryChipRow` is a fixed `HStack` with no wrap and no horizontal scroll, and neither chip's `Text(category.displayName)` carries `.fixedSize`. At the largest accessibility size `.subheadline` scales roughly 15pt → ~42pt; "Eat & Drink" and "Things to do" plus two checkmarks plus 28pt of horizontal padding each is well over 600pt against a ~393pt width, so both labels compress and truncate. `qa`'s new `SearchRowGrowthGuardTests` sweeps for `.lineLimit(` and correctly finds none — but `.lineLimit` is not the mechanism here; `HStack` overflow is, and only `.fixedSize` prevents it. `SearchResultRow` has `.fixedSize` on both `Text` runs; `CategoryChip` has it on neither. **Stated as a code-read finding, not a live one** — `qa` could not force a content-size override in that session and neither could I, so this is reasoning from the layout, not an observed screenshot.
  5. **Four `architect` questions were routed to `product` at TRD §12 and are all ruled**, in the PRD's Decisions log: **D8 upheld** (a chip narrows *places*; a Hood match survives — req 3 says "narrows," a Hood carries no `PlaceCategory`, and dropping Hoods would make a chip delete a whole result kind); **D9 upheld** (two row words; a keyword hit is a Place row — req 2 bullet 2's own justification clause is a two-way distinction and req 8's VoiceOver examples give only two forms); **§4.10's undimmed MapKit base tiles accepted as a limitation** (the requirement is about the prominence of Passenger-authored content; `Map` exposes no layer to insert one into and a full-screen scrim would darken the matches); **D2 (0.45/0.92) accepted for Build Phase 1 and carried to Aviran**, whose call the layout is (§9 Q15) — the architect priced the reversal at two constants and one gesture, so nothing is locked. **Not ruled:** D10's underlying interrupted-vs-completed product rule (`ux-flows.md` §9 Q17) — flagged by `designer` as its own reconciliation rather than Aviran's call, so it stays Aviran's and is not `product`'s to close alone. The build matches the PRD as written either way.
  6. **Scope gate re-run on inherited work** (Job 0 item 4 — a task already in the pipeline gets the citation check the first time `product` touches it at a gate). Both Motivation quotes verified **verbatim** against `strategy/passenger-strategy.md`: the "Search + quick filters… search filters the map, it doesn't bypass it" line at strategy line 47, and the "surfaced as **quick filters** inside the search sheet" line at line 36. Authorized V1 scope. No social surface, no onboarding, no Phase-2/3 hooks anywhere in `Search/` or `SearchSheet/`. **Data/schema need** (Job 1 item 7): already explicit and already owned — `places.keywords` is specified in `places-dataset` req 4 with the probe list as T-042 step B4, and the PRD's Technical design states the three matched fields by name. Nothing to fix on that pass.
- **Verdict: REJECT.** Back to `build`, `ios-developer`. Fix F1; fold in F2. Fix *direction* deliberately not prescribed — emphasising a matched place's own Hood is the obvious candidate (`SearchIndex.PlaceEntry` already carries both `hoodName` and `place.hoodID`, so the data is in hand), but ungating matched pins from `showsNames` or moving the camera are live alternatives and the call is `architect`/`ios-developer`'s.
- **Evidence:** all greps and line numbers above run against `passenger-code` current `main` and cross-checked at `3d8e3b8`; `git show --stat 3d8e3b8`, `git diff --stat 3d8e3b8..HEAD`. No build or test run was needed to establish F1 — it follows from two constants in shipped source (`MapZoomTier.closeSpanThreshold = 0.06`, `telAvivCityWide` span `0.14`) and one `if` at `MapScreen.swift:244`.

### 2026-08-03 — data-engineer — T-034/PAS-25: §4.2 query amendment confirmed correct as written

- **Did:** closed the last outstanding item from `product`'s 2026-08-03 acceptance pass on T-034 (the "D1 CONCUR" paragraph names `data-engineer` as still owing this). Read this file's T-034/T-035/T-036 acceptance entry (the "D1 CONCUR" paragraph) and `prds/live-events-overlay/TRD.md` §4.2 directly, per the dispatch brief — did not act on the summary alone. The ask: confirm (or fix) whether §4.2's query, as amended (dropping `start_at=gte.{anchorHour}`), actually implements the corrected **overlap** semantics D1 settled — "an event is visible if it overlaps the selected hour," not "starts within it" — rather than assume the amendment's own stated rationale is sufficient proof. This is a Build Phase 1 design-correctness check; no live query runs yet (T-043's pipeline is unbuilt), so verification is against the TRD's stated query shape only.
- **Verified by derivation, not by re-reading the amendment's own argument as its own proof.** §4.3's client-side predicate renders event at bucket `k` iff `startAt < bucketEnd(k) && endAt > bucketStart(k) && endAt > now`. Taking the union of that predicate over all 13 buckets (`k = 0…12`) that the client ever evaluates, the necessary-and-sufficient *superset* condition the fetch must satisfy collapses to exactly two bounds: `startAt < anchorHour + 13h` (from `k=12`'s `bucketEnd`) and `endAt > anchorHour` (from `k=0`'s `bucketStart`). Checked the amended query against that derived pair term for term: the query's own `start_at=lt.{anchorHour+13h}` matches the upper bound exactly, and `events_public`'s standing `end_at > now()` filter matches the lower bound given `anchorHour ≈ now()` at fetch time (session load or hour-roll refresh per §4.6/D11 — never more than seconds apart, immaterial at hour granularity). **Confirmed: the query as amended is correct.** The dropped `start_at=gte.{anchorHour}` clause was strictly tighter than the derived lower bound — it constrained `startAt` where the correct bound constrains `endAt` — so it necessarily excluded in-progress-at-open-time events (an event that started before `anchorHour` and is still running), which is exactly the failure mode D1's own rationale names. This confirms the drop was *necessary* for overlap semantics to be reachable at all, not merely a harmless simplification. No under-fetch found: every event that could satisfy the overlap predicate at any `k` survives the amended fetch. Rows the query returns that don't end up rendering at the currently-selected `k` are trimmed by §4.3's predicate client-side, which is correctness-neutral (over-fetch, not under-fetch). No SQL, view, index, or RLS policy implication follows from this — the view's existing filters were already doing the real work; the amendment only removes a redundant, over-tight client-side constraint.
- **No fix needed.** Nothing in T-043's `events_public` view or `live-events-pipeline/TRD.md` §4.2 changes as a result of this confirmation.
- **TRD edit:** added a confirmation note to `prds/live-events-overlay/TRD.md` §4.2 (immediately below the amendment paragraph, carrying the derivation above) and updated §11's `data-engineer` sign-off bullet from "to confirm at review" to "CONFIRMED correct as written, 2026-08-03." No requirement, contract, schema, or build step changed — this is the same class of documentation-only reconciliation as T-042's v2 amendment (no re-review owed).
- **Board:** updated both `BOARD.md` T-034 rows (Tasks table and V1 Build Phases table) to record the confirmation and point at the TRD note; T-034's acceptance status (`aviran-review`, PARTIAL reqs 1-5, req 6 → T-050) is otherwise unaffected — this closes only the one outstanding confirmation, not the task.
- **Left behind:** nothing new. T-050 (req 6 toggle + 400ms re-verification), T-051 (fixture bucket-5 plausibility fix), and T-052 (design-spec/raw-slug gaps) remain open and unaffected by this pass, per the acceptance entry above.

### 2026-08-03 — product — T-049/PAS-37 ruling: bundled-vs-fetched `place_type` registry — **amend T-042 to match T-037 D4 (option 2)**

- **Did:** documentation-reconciliation ruling dispatched by `chief-of-staff` (round 4, relay). Read `BOARD.md` in full (T-037/T-042/T-049 rows), this file's recent worklog (no "Current Snapshot" section exists — the documented exception at `PROGRESS.md:830`), then **both disputed sections in full and their surrounding documents**: `prds/passport/TRD.md` §1 open-items table, §2.1, §3.3, §3.4/D4, §11 A1, §12; `prds/places-dataset/TRD.md` §2.2, §3.1, §3.3, §4.2, §4.4, §4.5, §5, §9, §10. Did **not** rule from the ticket description's summary of either.
- **Verdict — option 2. The registry is bundled; `GET /rest/v1/place_types` comes out of T-042's client fetch contract.** Three independent grounds, any one sufficient:
  1. **Scope ownership.** T-042 §2.2 assigns the client half of C-STICKER-1 to T-037 by name, and §9 states *"No `[iOS]` step exists in this task — every client-side consequence is another task's amendment."* §4.5's *"One extra small GET for `place_types` … fetched once per session alongside the places load"* is a client-runtime behaviour claim inside a document that says it specs no client behaviour. D4 governs by scope, not by which doc ships or gets referenced last.
  2. **T-042 already contradicts itself, and its own §4.2 sides with D4.** §4.2 defines the client half as *"a test asserting every `sticker_shape` present in the shipped `place-types.json` **export** resolves to a real asset."* A shipped export is a bundled build-time artifact — D4's design, written into T-042 three sections before §4.5 specs a runtime GET. Amending §4.5 makes T-042 self-consistent; amending D4 would leave T-042 contradicting itself and break §4.2's own falsifiable pass condition, which is only checkable against a bundled file.
  3. **D4's argument is unrebutted and nothing needs the GET.** A `sticker_shape` key is undrawable unless the binary ships the asset; an unknown key renders `.generic` however it arrived, so fetching buys an undrawable key plus a request, a cache field and a skew class. Both `data-engineer` and `code-reviewer` APPROVEd A1/A2 and flagged only the unreconciled-docs process gap, neither contested the reasoning. T-042 names no consumer of that endpoint: the pipeline runs authored source → validator → export → DB seed, so the DB is downstream of the mapping, never upstream of it.
- **Options 1 and 3 rejected explicitly, not by omission.** (1) "Intentionally different concerns" is not a coherent story here — one client, one registry, one mapping; "the server offers it and the client never calls it" is a dead endpoint documented as a contract, which is what gets built by whoever reads §4.5 without reading passport §3.4. (3) Phase-2-scoping is worse than doing nothing: D4 is explicitly *not* Build-Phase scoped (*"it holds permanently for V1"*), and deferring parks the contradiction at the precise moment nobody re-reads this ticket, handing the Phase-2 developer two approved docs that still disagree.
- **No code change, confirmed against source not assumed.** T-037's in-flight build is building D4 as written — A1 already landed (`passenger-code cc2b008`, `Passenger/Resources/place-types-tel-aviv.json`, six types, bundled). T-042 is HELD/undispatched. Nothing already shipped moves.
- **Second finding — new, not in `PAS-37`'s description: the bundled registry has no emitter, and until now had two names.** The shipped `place-types-tel-aviv.json` header reads *"Regenerate/replace, do not extend by hand"* — and **no generator exists that could regenerate it.** Verified directly: `database/scripts/` holds `build_hoods.py`, `export_hoods_geojson.py`, `validate_dataset.py`, `test_hood_containment_fixture.py` — no `export_places.py` (T-042 B3, unbuilt), no `places-tel-aviv.source.json`. T-042 §4.2 calls the artifact an "export," implying generated; T-042's build breakdown emits only `places-tel-aviv.json` + the DB seed. At Phase 2, when B1's vocabulary is ratified and `place_types` holds real rows, the bundle and the table can diverge with nothing detecting it, and whoever updates the bundle hand-edits a file the TRD calls an export — **L-024's exact failure mode, one phase away, with a hand-edit ban already printed in the file's own header and no way to obey it.** Reconciling §4.5 without closing this just moves the hole. ### 2026-08-03 — designer — design-principles.md §6: corrected the PAS-36 citation, added carve-out

- **Did:** dispatched by `chief-of-staff` (this run) to fix a follow-on problem in `design/design-principles.md` §6, "Presentation exclusivity — never stack two modal surfaces": that section (added by an earlier `designer` pass the same day) cited `PAS-36` as its evidencing example of a violation. `chief-of-staff` had since re-diagnosed `PAS-36` and found the diagnosis didn't hold — `prds/places-been-saved/TRD.md` §4.6/§5 (approved, `trd-review`-cleared) explicitly designs for the exact state `PAS-36` reported: a place-detail sheet opened by a row tap inside the still-presented Places list, with the list staying underneath and reappearing on dismiss (`router.placeDepth == 1`, derived — no `entryPath` field added). Read §4.6 and §5 directly before touching anything, plus `MapChromeState.swift`'s `NavSurface`/`toggle()` to confirm the exclusivity mechanism the section was pointing at.
- **Change made — kept the general rule, fixed the citation, added an explicit carve-out (option (a) of the two offered):**
  - Rewrote the "Rule" statement itself so it no longer flatly contradicts the carve-out: it now scopes "never co-presented" to **independently-reachable** top-level surfaces, not any two surfaces visible at once.
  - Added a **Carve-out** paragraph: a surface opened *from within* another surface it doesn't need to dismiss (parent stays presented, child renders above it, dismissing the child reveals the parent unchanged) is a parent/child pair, not two competing surfaces — cites `TRD.md` §4.6's `placeDepth == 1` derivation and its own line, *"the modal renders above the list; dismissing it reveals the list unchanged."*
  - Added a **Corrected 2026-08-03** paragraph stating plainly that `PAS-36` was previously cited as a violation and that diagnosis didn't hold, why (TRD §4.6 designs for exactly that state on purpose), and that **no other confirmed evidencing example currently exists in this codebase** — the rule is kept anyway because it's still independently supported by T-036 D8's own reasoning about *unintended* co-presentation (an orphaned sheet, or opening one surface without closing another first), which is a real, distinct failure mode from the parent/child case.
  - Reworded the D8 citation and the "Checkable at spec/review time" paragraph to match: D8 means never *orphaned* co-presence, not "never simultaneously on screen at all"; a reviewer checking for a §6 finding should first ask whether the second surface was opened from within the first (carve-out, not a finding) before treating stacked surfaces as a breach.
  - Removed the bare `**Cite:** PAS-36.` line — folded into the corrected paragraph instead.
- **Left as-is, considered and rejected:** narrowing the rule's scope (option (b)) — rejected because the general "no orphaned/accidental co-presentation" guidance is still sound and still has a real mechanism (`DetailRouter`, `MapChromeState.NavSurface`) behind it; narrowing would have thrown out guidance that's still correct along with the one bad citation. Did not touch §7's reviewer checklist line referencing §6 — it already says "check for a single 'what's presented' state," which still reads correctly once §7's own text is read against the new carve-out (a reviewer checking that heuristic will naturally ask the carve-out's question). Did not generate an `.html` twin — checked precedent first: no other file in `design/` (including the phase-1 design docs and this same file's original add) has one except `ux-flows.md`/`.html`, so this isn't an established convention for `design-principles.md`.
- **Flagging outside this task's scope, not acted on:** this session's dispatch brief said `PAS-36`'s shipped behavior (list stays under the place sheet) is TRD-approved intentional design. But `PROGRESS.md`'s own recent entries (2026-08-03, `ios-developer` and `chief-of-staff`, `PAS-36` fix `passenger-code 4cd55f8`, `ios-code-reviewer` APPROVE) show a *different*, concurrent session already shipped a fix that does the opposite — `chrome` is now dismissed alongside `detailRouter.openPlace(place)`, so the list **no longer** stays presented under the sheet, and that change has already cleared code review and moved to `qa`. That looks like two concurrent chief-of-staff threads reaching opposite conclusions about whether `PAS-36`'s reported state is a bug — one shipped a fix reverting the TRD-approved co-presentation, the other (this one) concluded the co-presentation was correct all along. ### 2026-08-03 — ios-developer — PAS-36 fix: Places list stays co-presented with place-detail sheet

- **Did:** fixed the bug dispatched by `chief-of-staff`'s hilos intake (entry immediately below). Read this file's Current Snapshot/recent worklog and `passenger-code/CLAUDE.md` first, per protocol.
- **Root cause: confirmed as diagnosed, not corrected.** Independently re-read `PlacesListOverlay.swift`, `MapScreen.swift`'s overlay/sheet wiring (lines 231-243, 358-385), `MapChromeState.swift`, `DetailRouter.swift`, and `MapScreenTests.swift` before touching anything. The dispatch's root cause is exactly right: `PlacesListOverlay` renders as a z5 `.overlay` gated on `chrome.presented == .places` (`MapScreen.swift:235`); its `onSelect` closure (`MapScreen.swift:238`, pre-fix) called `detailRouter.openPlace(place)` only, never `chrome`. `DetailRouter.openPlace` flips `isDepth1Presented` to `true`, opening the system `.sheet` at Site A (`MapScreen.swift:243`) for `PlaceDetailModal`. Because `chrome.presented` never changes value (it was already `.places`, stays `.places`), `.onChange(of: chrome.presented)` (`MapScreen.swift:312`) never fires, so `handlePresentedSurfaceChange` — the function that already closes a stranded place modal on the other two D8 transitions — never runs for this third one. The list overlay and the place-detail sheet render simultaneously, violating T-036's own TRD D8 invariant. Confirmed `MapScreenTests.swift` had no coverage for this path before this fix (only `openPlacesListClosesHood` and both directions of `handlePresentedSurfaceChange` existed).
- **Fix:** `Passenger/Map/MapScreen.swift` — added `static func selectPlaceFromList(router: DetailRouter, chrome: MapChromeState, place: Place)`, alongside the existing `openPlacesList`/`handlePresentedSurfaceChange` static functions (same pure, unit-testable-without-a-live-SwiftUI-environment pattern this file already uses for D8 wiring). It calls `router.openPlace(place)` then `chrome.dismiss()`. `PlacesListOverlay`'s `onSelect` closure now calls this instead of `detailRouter.openPlace(place)` directly. This makes the list-row-tap path an explicit dismiss rather than relying on the `onChange` hook, which structurally can't catch it (selecting a row isn't a surface transition — `chrome.presented` doesn't change).
- **Prevention (what stops this recurring):** added `PassengerTests/MapScreenTests.swift`'s `MapScreenD8WiringTests.selectingPlaceFromListDismissesList` — sets `chrome.toggle(.places)`, calls `MapScreen.selectPlaceFromList(router:chrome:place:)`, and asserts `chrome.presented != .places` and `router.place?.id == place.id`. This is a real regression guard: it fails against the pre-fix code (which never touched `chrome`) and passes against the fix, sitting in the same suite and same style as the other two D8-invariant tests so a future change to this wiring is checked by the same mechanism.

If a `VisitEvent` arrives before the persisted ledger loads, `LocalQAGate.decide` sees an empty `answeredPlaceIDs`/`nil lastAskedAt`, so a place answered in a prior session could get re-asked. Currently masked in Phase 1 only because the sole trigger, `DebugVisitSource`, has a hardcoded ~1s post-launch delay that comfortably outlasts a single JSON read — but `start()`/`handle()` is the exact code Phase 2's real triggers (`foregroundArrival`/`notificationTap`) will run through unchanged, and those can fire at any point after cold launch. Fix: sequence the two calls in one `.task` (`await loadPersistedState()` then `await start()`) rather than racing them.
  2. **`Passenger/Detail/PlaceDetailModal.swift:80-86`** (`touristTrapSlot`) — hand-builds `HStack { Image(systemName: "camera.fill"); Text(...) }` instead of `Label(_:systemImage:)`, breaking the pattern every other icon+text row in this diff's own neighborhood uses (`categoryRow` two lines above it, `PlacesListRow`'s "Permanently closed" badge, `HoodButton`, `EventDetailModal`'s rows, `HoodSheet`'s error row, `CachedDataIndicator` — all `Label` or `Label` + explicit `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)`). A raw `Image(systemName:)` isn't hidden from the accessibility tree by default, so a VoiceOver user swiping the place-detail modal gets an extra, auto-labeled "camera" stop before "Tourist-heavy spot" — a redundant announcement none of the sibling rows produce. Fix: `Label(FlagCopy.placeLine, systemImage: "camera.fill").foregroundStyle(Color("Flag"))`.
